title: DNA Extraction from Trichuris trichiura Worm Samples
author: James Owen Delaluna

After washing, snap-freeze samples in liquid nitrogen.

Step 7: DNA Quantification and Quality Assessment

steps.title: Transfer worm samples to tube
steps.instruction: Transfer adult Trichuris trichiura worms (preserved in formaldehyde or ethanol) into a clean microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Wash samples with PBS
steps.instruction: Add sterile PBS to fully immerse the worms, then remove PBS; repeat the wash 2–3 times to eliminate residual formaldehyde or ethanol.

steps.title: Excise anterior worm portion
steps.instruction: If worms are intact, excise and retain only the anterior portion to ensure consistency across samples.

steps.title: Add stainless steel beads
steps.instruction: Place the washed sample into a tube containing 2–4 small stainless steel beads.

steps.title: Add lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Add the appropriate lysis buffer supplied with the Clear‑S kit to the tube.

steps.title: Homogenize with TissueLyser
steps.instruction: Homogenize the bead‑sample mixture in a TissueLyser LT at 50 Hz for 1 minute per cycle, performing 2–3 cycles.

steps.title: Extended lysis incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the lysate for the standard time specified by the Clear‑S kit, then extend the incubation by an additional 10–20 minutes to improve DNA recovery.

steps.title: Perform DNA extraction
steps.instruction: Proceed with DNA extraction using the Clear‑S Quick DNA Extraction Kit, following the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Elute the purified DNA in nuclease‑free water or the elution buffer provided with the kit.

steps.title: Quantify DNA
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration and purity using a Nanodrop spectrophotometer; record concentration (ng/µL) and A260/A280 ratio. Concentration should be >10–20 ng/µL for downstream applications such as long‑range PCR (β‑tubulin ~4.2 kb) or ITS2 amplification (~481 bp).

steps.title: Store extracted DNA
steps.instruction: Store the extracted DNA at –20 °C for short‑term use or at –80 °C for long‑term storage.
